title: Does a ₹1,000 SIP a Month Actually Build Wealth? The Honest Math
summary: A ₹1,000 monthly SIP grows to roughly ₹2.3 lakh in 10 years at 12% returns. Here’s what SIP actually delivers for Indian investors, and when it falls short.
content:
Yes, SIP works. But whether ₹1,000 a month works for you depends on what you’re expecting it to do, and most articles skip the honest part. A ₹1,000 monthly SIP in a broad equity fund, held for 10 years, typically grows to around ₹2.3 lakh at 12% annual returns. That beats an FD. It’s not enough for retirement on its own. And it’s a perfectly reasonable place to start, as long as you know what you’re actually building.

Key Takeaways

  • A ₹1,000 monthly SIP grows to roughly ₹2.3 lakh in 10 years at 12% annual returns, better than a fixed deposit but not retirement money by itself.
  • SIP beats a 7% fixed deposit after about five years, but only if you hold through the bad stretches.
  • A step-up SIP (raising contributions 10% annually) can grow your 20-year corpus by around 45% more than a flat SIP.
  • Don’t use SIP for money you might need within three years. Equity funds have lost money in roughly 40% of 3-year stretches historically.
  • The amount you invest matters more than which fund you pick when starting out.

What Does ₹1,000 a Month Actually Grow To?

At 12% annual returns, a ₹1,000 monthly SIP reaches roughly ₹2.3 lakh after 10 years and around ₹10 lakh after 20. The first decade looks modest. The second decade does most of the real work, because compound growth takes time to build real speed.

Monthly SIPAfter 10 YearsAfter 20 Years
₹1,000₹2.3 lakh₹10 lakh
₹5,000₹11.6 lakh₹50 lakh
₹10,000₹23.2 lakh₹1 crore

Assumes 12% CAGR, monthly compounding. Past returns don’t guarantee future performance.

So ₹1,000 a month is a real start. Just know it won’t fund a retirement on its own unless you’re starting young and staying invested for 25 to 30 years. If you can get to ₹5,000 a month, the 20-year numbers get genuinely interesting. At ₹10,000 for 20 years, you’re near ₹1 crore. That’s where SIP earns the headlines it usually gets.

Does SIP Beat a Fixed Deposit in India?

Over five or more years, equity SIP has historically beaten FD returns after taxes in India. A 7% FD earns about 4.9% per year post-tax at the 30% bracket. Equity SIP averages roughly 11% post-tax over a decade or more, after the 12.5% long-term capital gains tax on profits above ₹1.25 lakh each year.

FeatureEquity SIPBank FD (7%)
Avg. gross return~12% (historical)7%
Post-tax return (30% bracket)~11%~4.9%
Capital guaranteedNoYes
Lock-inNone1 to 5 years typically
Best suited forGoals 5+ years awayGoals under 3 years

The catch with FD: inflation in India runs around 4 to 5% annually. A post-tax return of 4.9% barely keeps pace. SIP, over a long enough period, has cleared that margin by a meaningful amount in nearly every rolling period since 2000.

If you’re in the 20% tax bracket, the FD picture improves a bit (around 5.6% post-tax), but SIP still wins over 10 years in most historical periods.

When Is SIP the Wrong Choice?

SIP doesn’t work for money you might need within three years. Equity funds can and do fall, and a forced sale into a down market wipes out the gains SIP is meant to build. Short-term savings, emergency funds, and high-interest debt repayment all take priority over starting a SIP.

Say you’re saving for a car in 18 months, or a wedding two years out. Don’t put that in equity SIP. Funds have lost money in roughly 40% of all 3-year stretches between 2000 and 2020. You don’t want to be forced to sell into a market that’s down 30%.

Being definately clear on your time horizon is more important than which fund you pick. Short-term money in an equity fund is a mismatch between the tool and the job.

Also wrong for SIP: your emergency fund. Keep three to six months of expenses in a savings account or short-term FD, accessible without checking NAV first.

One more case. If you’re carrying high-interest debt at 14 to 18%, no SIP return justifies paying that interest in parallel. Pay the debt first.

What Is a Step-Up SIP, and Does It Actually Help?

A step-up SIP automatically raises your monthly contribution by a fixed percentage each year. At a 10% annual step-up, a ₹10,000 starting SIP reaches roughly ₹1.45 crore after 20 years, versus ₹1 crore with a flat SIP. That’s a 45% difference from one setting in your fund app at setup time.

Ten percent per year is the most commonly recommended rate, matching typical salary increments in India’s corporate sector. The principle works accross all major fund platforms, and activating it is straightforward once you’re in your fund account.

Apps like Groww and INDmoney let you configure the step-up at no extra cost. Set it when you first start the SIP. If you’re already running one without a step-up, you can modify it anytime through your fund platform.

Frequently Asked Questions About SIP in India

Can I withdraw SIP money anytime?

Yes. Most open-ended equity mutual funds allow redemption any business day, with the amount reaching your bank within 2 to 3 business days. There’s no lock-in. But redeeming during a market downturn locks in those losses, which is why SIP works best when you stay invested through corrections rather than react to them.

Is SIP safe for complete beginners?

Equity SIP carries market risk and can lose value in the short run. For a first investment, a Nifty 50 index fund is a reasonable choice: lower volatility than mid-cap funds and a long performance track record. Avoid sector or thematic funds until you understand how they move in different market conditions.

What’s the tax rule on SIP gains in 2026?

Gains on equity mutual funds held over one year are taxed at 12.5% as long-term capital gains. The first ₹1.25 lakh of long-term gains per financial year is exempt. Gains on units sold within 12 months attract 20% short-term capital gains tax. Each SIP installment counts as a separate purchase with its own holding period for tax purposes.

Should I SIP into a mutual fund or just buy a Nifty 50 ETF?

A Nifty 50 ETF SIP tracks the same index at a lower expense ratio (roughly 0.05 to 0.10%) compared to active large-cap funds (0.5 to 1%). If you have a demat account, ETF SIP is marginally cheaper. Without one, a Nifty 50 index mutual fund through Zerodha Coin or Groww works just as well for most people.

What if I miss a SIP installment?

Missing one payment doesn’t cancel your SIP. Most fund houses skip that month’s deduction and resume the next. If your account lacks sufficient funds for three or more consecutive months, the SIP may pause automatically. The fix: set your debit date one or two days after your salary credit date so the balance is always there.

The Short Version

SIP works. The key variables are your investment amount and your time horizon. If you can get to ₹5,000 a month with an annual step-up, the 20-year numbers start looking like actual wealth. Past returns vary, and this post is information, not personal financial advice.
